harness: repo char-LM parity gate (memory-native-charlm), same architecture/data/tokenizer/init/budget per kind; tinyshakespeare char corpus (vocab 65), config=tiny (4 layers, d=256, block=128, 4 heads), batch 32, 600 steps, eval 20 iters

time_to_quality.note: val loss vs wall-clock for dense vs counter_rms, seed 0, same budget per run; each row is a separate run with the given number of steps
time_to_quality.ratio_time_to_equal_quality_estimate: ~2.1x slower (14-16 s vs 7 s) but then overtakes dense quality (1.97 vs 2.15 at 600 steps)

honest_read: Counter variants reach equal or better val loss at the same step budget with 3.7-3.8x less persistent state, but the char-LM gate runs them 4x slower per token (84k vs 334-376k tok/s) because the GPT model uses the plain counter layers, not the fast group-scale packed path measured in the layer benchmark. Peak VRAM at this model scale is activation-dominated: only 1.05-1.12x less.
